title: Stratified Judge Ensemble and Cohort Calibration Playbook for Config-Linked Regressions
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: Model and configuration (quantization, temperature, KV cache policy, batching) changes frequently trigger noisy eval signals. Current LLM-as-judge workflows produce verdicts that shift with even small config deltas, which leads to either (a) noisy regression alerts that waste engineering cycles or (b) missed subtle quality degradations because we normalize across heterogeneous cohorts. We need a repeatable scoring methodology that ties judge behavior to config strata and produces calibrated, explainable regression signals that can be actioned by runtime, model-ops, and PM teams.

Proposal summary: Develop a stratified judge-ensemble and per-cohort calibration playbook. Key elements: (1) Partition evaluation corpus into config-strata (e.g., short/long context, high-ambiguity prompts, numeric reasoning subset, heavy-tokenization cases). (2) Use an ensemble of judges (diverse LLMs and a deterministic rubric-based scorer) and compute per-judge calibration curves per cohort. (3) Apply a lightweight calibration layer (isotonic/regression or temperature-scaling of judge logits) per cohort so ensemble scores are comparable across configs. (4) Introduce confidence-aware aggregation: weight judge votes by calibrated confidence in the target cohort. (5) Add attribution heuristics to map regression deltas to likely causes (model weight change vs quantization vs runtime kernel change). (6) Define alerting thresholds driven by cohort-weighted effect sizes and minimum cohort sample sizes to reduce false positives.

Why this is different: Instead of a single global judge calibration, we intentionally treat judge behavior as conditional on workload strata. This reduces judge-model mismatch when we evaluate a config variant that accentuates certain failure modes (e.g., long-sequence KV-cache hot paths). The ensemble plus per-cohort calibration balances sensitivity and robustness and makes signals actionable for specific engineering owners.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Demonstrated reduction in operator noise: 40% drop in manual triage events for eval regressions during a 6-week pilot. (2) Maintain or improve true-positive detection for injected degradations (target sensitivity >= 90% for synthetic regressions at >=1.5% absolute quality drop within cohorts). (3) Provide per-regression attribution with confidence score >= 0.7 for >= 60% of detected regressions. (4) Integrate an automated regression alert into the Console with cohort-level breakdown and a link to the top-3 suspected causes.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Definition and tooling (2 sprints): define cohort taxonomy, build cohort assignment tool for existing eval datasets, and surface cohort metadata in our eval harness.
2) Judge ensemble baseline (2 sprints): select 3 judge models (one small deterministic rubric, one medium open model, one high-quality LLM), implement ensembling, and collect judgment traces across cohorts.
3) Calibration layer & statistics (2 sprints): implement per-cohort calibration (isotonic/regression) and establish statistical tests (bootstrap CIs, effect sizes) for regressions.
4) Alerting & Console integration (1 sprint): wire cohort-weighted alerts to Console, include drilldowns with judge ensemble breakdown and suggested rollback/fallback actions.
5) Pilot & retro (2 sprints): run pilot on 10 active config rollouts and iterate acceptance thresholds.

Metrics to track: cohort sample size distribution, per-judge calibration error (Brier score / ECE) per cohort, precision/recall on synthetic injections, triage load (human-hours), time-to-detect, and time-to-assign.

Rollout & risk mitigation: Start with internal-only audits for config changes tagged as "experimental". For high-impact runtime patches (e.g., kernel or quantization changes), require parallel evaluation against anchor baselines and a staging hold until ensemble confirms no regression with 95% CI. Risk: false reassurance if cohorts are too coarse; mitigation: iterative refinement and mandatory minimum sample counts for any cohort-based alert.

Stakeholders: PM (product-management), Research/Applied ML, Serving runtime ENG, Infra SRE, Console UX, Customer Success (for high-severity regressions).
comments: 2025-01-15 Aisha Raman: Initial draft of playbook uploaded. Asking ENG and Research to review cohort taxonomy and judge candidate list.
2025-01-21 Daniel Park (Research): Reviewed. Suggest adding a deterministic rubric scorer for numeric/outcome-stable tasks to anchor ensemble. Also recommended bootstrap-based CIs for small cohorts.

2025-01-28 Maria Chen (Serving ENG): Flagged dependency: we need per-request metadata from runtime (quantization flag, kernel variant, batch_id) to reliably assign requests into cohorts. Opening ENG-21590 to add metadata hooks.
2025-02-04 Carlos Vega (assignee): Proposed experiment plan and dataset split. Draft PR for eval harness changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/514 (WIP).

2025-02-12 Olivia Reyes (Console UX): Mockups for alert drilldown posted: https://drive.google.com/mockups/stratified-alerts (link). UX suggests including top-3 suspect causes and per-cohort judge vote breakdown.

2025-02-20 Research sync notes: Agreed on judges: deterministic-rubric-v1, open-judge-llama-2-13b, redwood-judge-gptx (internal). Calibration approach: isotonic for small cohorts, logistic scaling for larger cohorts. Decision to use minimum cohort size = 250 samples for automatic alerts; smaller cohorts will create 'investigate' flags.

2025-02-25 Security review request: QA asked whether judged content could leak PII during debug. Security review requested (tracking): SEC-0581. Security guidance: sanitize logs and redact sensitive spans before sending to third-party judges.
